1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Nc3 c5 5.d.strategy: Adds a third defender to the d5-pawn and opens the f1-bishop, which now attacks the c4-pawn. White is still a pawn down but gets the centre and quick development, and plays against Black's uncastled king.

Grabs a second pawn and opens the e-file, but the pawn on d5 is attacked three times and defended twice, and the king is still on e8. Black has to give material back or defend very precisely; the extra pawns are worth it only if development catches up.
